A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AgentSquare study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original six-task evaluations using GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o, component ablations, search trajectories and performance-predictor validation in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds search-cost and termination-iteration results in Table A.6.

M1.justification: The four-module architecture, evolution, recombination and performance predictor remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. Sections 3.5–3.6 clarify that evolved modules receive real-environment evaluation while recombinations use the predictor; they do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six tasks: WebShop, ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, M3ToolEval, TravelPlanner and PDDL. No dataset, domain or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and A.3 retain the same 12 hand-crafted agents, Random and Bayesian module-search baselines, and OPRO prompt-search baseline. Comparator membership in the other reported comparisons also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 and GPT-4o, matched few-shot example counts, random initialization and termination after five consecutive iterations without improvement. The added task-metric descriptions and trajectory-model attribution disclose settings rather than establish a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New Table A.6 supplements the existing agent-execution cost plots with an accounting of search overhead: average cost per iteration and iterations until termination across tasks and models. Component ablations, predictor validation, search trajectories and discovered-module case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Table A.6 averages costs over search iterations without introducing repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table A.6 adds concrete search-resource results, including GPT-4o WebShop cost of $10.51 per iteration over 15 iterations and ALFWorld cost of $13.96 over 18 iterations. Existing performance tables, ablation values and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The module definitions, MoLAS optimization formulation and Equations 1–4 are retained. The added descriptions of existing task metrics introduce no new formal result, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: modular agent search, evolution and recombination, efficient prediction, interpretable designs and an average 17.2% improvement over the best human designs.

C2.justification: Section 3.6 newly explains why prediction is unsuitable for evolved modules absent from the experience pool. Section 4.2 also qualifies the cost comparisons by explicitly excluding one-time search costs, citing module reuse and reporting search costs separately.

D1.justification: v2 removes the complete recombination, performance-predictor and module-evolution meta-prompts from v1 Figures A.15–A.17, without replacing them elsewhere in the PDF. This substantially reduces documentation of the three central LLM operations. Task metrics, predictor-use details and search-resource information are added; the repository link and discovered-module code examples remain.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to prior agent frameworks, prompt optimization and architecture search are unchanged. Citation punctuation changes do not add or remove cited research.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical and citation-format edits, expands the predictor and metric explanations, adds a cost-accounting qualification and updates appendix references. The main section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 redraws connections between search operations and the module and experience pools. v2 adds Table A.6, removes three meta-prompt panels and relocates several figures. The retained module examples are renumbered from A.18–A.23 to A.15–A.20; most visual content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through explicit task metrics, predictor applicability and separate search-cost reporting. However, removing all three central meta-prompt templates reduces reproducibility from the supplied paper. These material benefits and losses coexist, while the scientific results remain unchanged, leaving no reliably assessable net quality direction.
